messages:
mira: quick heads-up — on canary today saw large latency jitter tied to cudaMalloc spikes during KV-cache refill. nsys trace shows a burst of allocations (~200ms window) that coincides with a flurry of small kernel launches and then a long GEMM stall. attaching trace link: https://perfetto.company/trace/ab12c3

alex: Ugh, that sounds like arena fragmentation + thundering herd when many requests miss cache. Can you paste the nsys sample and the kernel timeline snapshot?

mira: pasted snippets below. basically: a bunch of cuMemAlloc/cuMemFree calls interleaved with tiny copy kernels (~5–10us) and then a ~40ms cublasSgemm. The allocator appears to block scheduling.

mira: ```
# nsys summary (top events)
cuMemAlloc  38 calls   120ms total
cuMemFree   36 calls    90ms total
copy.H2D    120 calls   6ms total
small-kernel 300 calls  15ms total
cublasGemm  4 calls    160ms total
# note: cuMemAlloc peaks right before each cublasGemm
```

ben: I ran a local nvprof and saw similar. With --kv-warmup=50 the first 20s have heavy alloc/free churn. When I preallocate a 512MB arena and sub-allocate from it the spike disappears and latency stable.

alex: That suggests our pool fallback path is getting exercised under concurrent misses. Are we triggering host-side serializations when the pool can't satisfy sizes?

mira: yes — pool currently does a naive global lock on large-allocation path. When multiple workers try to refill the pool we serialize calls into the driver. perfetto timeline (linked): https://perfetto.company/trace/cd34ef shows many threads in kernel_wait state during cuMemAlloc.

perf-bot: deploy/trace: 2026-03-02T12:07:34Z attached.

mira: Immediate mitigation I tried: 1) Increase arena default to 512MB, 2) slab allocator for power-of-two sizes, 3) batching pool refills off the hot path. Results: tail p99 latency dropped ~45% in the canary, and cudaMalloc time reduced from 120ms->12ms in the nsys window.

ben: Repro steps I used: start server with --kv-pool=on --kv-arena=256MB --concurrency=64, run warmup with synthetic workload (1000 distinct keys). nvprof cmd: 
```
nvprof --print-gpu-trace --profile-child-processes ./run_canary --kv-warmup=100
```
Observations: cuMemAlloc spikes align with cache miss rate going above 30%.

alex: Action items:
- implement lock-free slab for common sizes (mira)
- add a background pool-refill thread to avoid on-path allocation (ben)
- add perf test that measures cuMemAlloc time under various warmup rates (alex)
- add trace collection hook to annotate traces with kv-cache miss rates (infra-bot)

mira: I'll open the PR for slab allocator and include nsys/perfetto reproducer. Will also drop a small patch to bump arena default while we validate.

alex: For kernel selection side-note — the trace shows several tiny kernels launched for cache bookkeeping right before choosing cublas path. If we can coalesce bookkeeping kernels or move them to host-only accounting, we could reduce kernel launch overhead that interferes with large GEMM scheduling.

ben: +1. Also we should ensure our compile-time kernel-fusion pass doesn't emit tiny kernels for common fast-paths. I flagged a couple in the codegen review.

mira: TL;DR: root cause is allocator contention + fragmentation during KV cache refill -> triggers many cuMemAlloc/cuMemFree -> kernel launch jitter -> long GEMM stalls. Fix path: pool/slab + background refill + default arena bump. Canary numbers look good. Follow-up run scheduled tomorrow with 10k warmup to validate long-run fragmentation. :thumbsup:
